module TopModule (
    input  logic clk,
    input  logic j,
    input  logic k,
    output logic Q
);

    always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
        case ({j, k})
            2'b00: Q <= Q;       // Hold state (Qold)
            2'b01: Q <= 1'b0;    // Reset
            2'b10: Q <= 1'b1;    // Set
            2'b11: Q <= ~Q;      // Toggle
        endcase
    end

endmodule

Prob076_always_case.code:
module TopModule (
    input  [2:0] sel,
    input  [3:0] data0,
    input  [3:0] data1,
    input  [3:0] data2,
    input  [3:0] data3,
    input  [3:0] data4,
    input  [3:0] data5,
    output [3:0] out
);

    // 6-to-1 multiplexer with 4-bit data and 3-bit select
    // When sel is in range [0, 5], output the corresponding data input.
    // When sel is out of range (i.e., 6 or 7), output 4'b0.
    assign out = (sel >= 3'b110) ? 4'b0 :
                 (sel == 3'b000) ? data0 :
                 (sel == 3'b001) ? data1 :
                 (sel == 3'b010) ? data2 :
                 (sel == 3'b011) ? data3 :
                 (sel == 3'b100) ? data4 :
                 data5;

endmodule

module TopModule (
    input  a,
    input  b,
    input  c,
    input  d,
    output q
);

    // Combinational logic derived from the truth table
    assign q = (a & b & c & d) |
               (a & b & c & !d) |
               (a & b & !c) |
               (a & !b & c & !d) |
               (a & !b & c & d) |
               (!a & b & c & !d) |
               (!a & b & c & d) |
               (!a & !b & c);

endmodule

Prob138_2012_q2fsm.code:
module TopModule (
    input  clk,
    input  reset,
    input  w,
    output z
);

    // State encoding: 2 bits
    // A = 2'b00, B = 2'b01, C = 2'b10, D = 2'b11, E = 2'b01, F = 2'b10
    // (Only 5 states used, but 2 bits allows easy encoding)
    
    reg [1:0] state, next_state;

    // State table / next-state logic (combinational)
    always @(*) begin
        case (state)
            2'b00: begin // State A
                if (w == 1'b1) next_state = 2'b01; // A --1--> B
                else           next_state = 2'b00; // A --0--> A
            end
            2'b01: begin // State B
                if (w == 1'b1) next_state = 2'b10; // B --1--> C
                else           next_state = 2'b11; // B --0--> D
            end
            2'b10: begin // State C
                if (w == 1'b1) next_state = 2'b01; // C --1--> E
                else           next_state = 2'b11; // C --0--> D
            end
            2'b11: begin // State D
                if (w == 1'b1) next_state = 2'b10; // D --1--> F
                else           next_state = 2'b00; // D --0--> A
            end
            default: next_state = 2'b00; // Should not happen
        endcase
    end

    // State flip-flops (sequential, positive edge triggered)
    always @(posedge clk) begin
        if (reset == 1'b1) begin
            state <= 2'b00; // Reset to state A
        end else begin
            state <= next_state;
        end
    end

    // Output logic (continuous assignment)
    // Output z is asserted (1) when in state E (2'b01)
    assign z = (state == 2'b01) ? 1'b1 : 1'b0;

endmodule

module TopModule (
    input  a,
    input  b,
    input  c,
    input  d,
    input  e,
    output [24:0] out
);

    // Assign the 25 comparison results.
    // Each bit is the XNOR (equality) of the corresponding pair of inputs.
    assign out[24] = ~a ^ a;          // a compared with a
    assign out[23] = ~a ^ b;          // a compared with b
    assign out[22] = ~a ^ c;          // a compared with c
    assign out[21] = ~a ^ d;          // a compared with d
    assign out[20] = ~a ^ e;          // a compared with e
    assign out[19] = ~b ^ a;          // b compared with a (same as out[23])
    assign out[18] = ~b ^ b;          // b compared with b
    assign out[17] = ~b ^ c;          // b compared with c
    assign out[16] = ~b ^ d;          // b compared with d
    assign out[15] = ~b ^ e;          // b compared with e
    assign out[14] = ~c ^ a;          // c compared with a
    assign out[13] = ~c ^ b;          // c compared with b
    assign out[12] = ~c ^ c;          // c compared with c
    assign out[11] = ~c ^ d;          // c compared with d
    assign out[10] = ~c ^ e;          // c compared with e
    assign out[9]  = ~d ^ a;          // d compared with a
    assign out[8]  = ~d ^ b;          // d compared with b
    assign out[7]  = ~d ^ c;          // d compared with c
    assign out[6]  = ~d ^ d;          // d compared with d
    assign out[5]  = ~d ^ e;          // d compared with e
    assign out[4]  = ~e ^ a;          // e compared with a
    assign out[3]  = ~e ^ b;          // e compared with b
    assign out[2]  = ~e ^ c;          // e compared with c
    assign out[1]  = ~e ^ d;          // e compared with d
    assign out[0]  = ~e ^ e;          // e compared with e

endmodule

module TopModule (
    input  [7:0] code,
    output [3:0] out,
    output       valid
);

    // Default assignments: outputs are 0 when no key is recognized
    assign valid = 1'b0;
    assign out   = 4'b0;

    // Combinational logic to decode scancodes
    always @(*) begin
        case (code)
            8'h45: begin out = 4'b0;   valid = 1'b1; end // Key 0
            8'h16: begin out = 4'b1;   valid = 1'b1; end // Key 1
            8'h1e: begin out = 4'b2;   valid = 1'b1; end // Key 2
            8'h26: begin out = 4'b3;   valid = 1'b1; end // Key 3
            8'h25: begin out = 4'b4;   valid = 1'b1; end // Key 4
            8'h2e: begin out = 4'b5;   valid = 1'b1; end // Key 5
            8'h36: begin out = 4'b6;   valid = 1'b1; end // Key 6
            8'h3d: begin out = 4'b7;   valid = 1'b1; end // Key 7
            8'h3e: begin out = 4'b8;   valid = 1'b1; end // Key 8
            8'h46: begin out = 4'b9;   valid = 1'b1; end // Key 9
            default: begin out = 4'b0; valid = 1'b0; end // No match
        endcase
    end

endmodule
